objective: Build a text adventure game in Python that is genuinely fun to play. The engine loads world data from YAML files defining rooms, items, NPCs, monsters, and connections. Implement a command parser handling movement (go north/south/east/west), inventory management (take, drop, use, examine), NPC interaction (talk to), combat commands (attack, flee), and look/status/help/quit. Add a turn-based combat system: the player has health and attack power, weapons and armor found in the world change combat stats when equipped, healing items can be used mid-fight, and monsters guard specific rooms and fight back with simple distinct behaviors. Include a final boss with two phases and a weakness to a special item hidden in the world — beating the boss wins the game, and dying ends the run with an honest defeat screen and the option to restart. Manage game state including player location, stats, equipment, inventory, room state changes, NPC dialogue progression, and defeated monsters. Support save and load of full game state to JSON. Create a playable demo world with at least 8 rooms, 5 items (including at least one weapon, one armor piece, one healing item, and the boss-weakness item), 2 NPCs with branching dialogue that hints at the boss weakness, 3 regular monsters, and the final boss. The game must be runnable from the command line, produce engaging descriptive text with clear combat narration, and be winnable in a reasonable playthrough by following the NPC hints.

Create world.yaml with content: A dark fantasy world where the player must defeat the Shadow Lich in its sanctum to save the realm. Include 9 rooms: Village Square (starting point), Elder's Hut, Whispering Forest, Hidden Cave, Ruined Library, Ancient Tower, Crystal Cavern, Throne Room (boss lair), and a Secret Garden. Place 6 items: Iron Sword (weapon), Leather Armor (armor), Healing Herb (healing), Crystal of Dawn (boss weakness), Ancient Key (opens Ruined Library), and a Magic Scroll (gives lore). Add 2 NPCs: Village Elder who speaks of the Lich's phylactery and hints that 'only dawn's light can banish the shadow', and a Hermit in the Whispering Forest who knows the Lich's two forms and that the Crystal of Dawn 'must be used at the moment of its vulnerability'. Include 3 regular monsters: Wolf Pack (forest), Cave Bat (cave), and Risen Skeleton (library) with simple aggressive behaviors. The final boss, Shadow Lich, guards the Throne Room and has two phases: first a spectral form that resists physical attacks, then a corporeal form that emerges after the player uses the Crystal of Dawn, where it becomes vulnerable to normal weapons. Defeating the Lich wins the game; dying shows a defeat screen with restart option.
Program starts cleanly and exits without errors
The game correctly loads and parses world.yaml to instantiate all rooms, items, NPCs, monsters, and room connections

goals.description: The Shadow Lich boss has two combat phases: its initial spectral form resists non-dawn attacks, and using the Crystal of Dawn during combat triggers its vulnerable corporeal form that takes normal weapon damage
Defeating the Shadow Lich displays a victory screen, player death displays a defeat screen with a restart option, and full game state can be saved to and loaded from JSON files without progress loss

notes.content:
Design the world schema as a strict YAML structure with top-level keys for rooms, items, npcs, and monsters, each entity referenced by a unique ID. Rooms should contain lists of exits with direction and target room IDs, plus optional lists of present items, NPCs, monsters, and state flags. Items need type tags (weapon, armor, healing, key) with numeric stats like attack_bonus, defense_bonus, and heal_amount. The command parser should normalize input to lowercase, split on spaces, and match the first token as a verb against a command map that includes movement verbs, interaction verbs, and combat verbs. For multi-object commands like "attack goblin with sword", implement a simple preposition detector that extracts the indirect object after "with" or "using". Support synonyms by mapping alternate verbs to canonical handlers, and always provide a "help" command that lists available verbs based on the current context (exploration vs combat).

Combat should run as an explicit state machine with phases: player_turn, monster_turn, and victory/defeat resolution. Track combat state separately from exploration state so the parser knows which command set to accept. Each monster needs a behavior script—simple conditional logic like "if health < 30% then flee" or "always attack strongest player weapon"—rather than random choice, making fights predictable but challenging. Equipment stats apply immediately when equipped and revert when unequipped; validate that weapons and armor occupy distinct slots. The boss requires a two-phase state transition triggered at a health threshold, with phase two using a different attack pattern and explicit vulnerability to the hidden item. When the boss is defeated, set a global victory flag; when player health reaches zero, enter a defeat state that displays a summary and offers a restart option that resets all state to initial values.

Serialize the entire game state to JSON using a single dictionary that includes player stats, location, inventory, equipment, room states (monster defeated flags, NPC dialogue progress), and global flags. Deserialize by reconstructing the world from YAML first, then overlaying the saved state to avoid stale references. Common pitfalls include mutating world data in place during gameplay, which corrupts save files—always copy mutable structures when loading. Test the parser with ambiguous input like "take" without an object or "go" without a direction; these should produce helpful error messages rather than crashes. Ensure NPC dialogue progresses based on player actions, not just conversation, so hints about the boss weakness feel earned. Finally, keep room descriptions concise but evocative, and narrate combat with clear hit/miss/fumble messages that include damage numbers and status effects, so players understand outcomes without rereading the state.

data_shapes.structure: Top-level mapping with 5 required keys: rooms (dict of room ID to room data), items (dict of item ID to item data), npcs (dict of NPC ID to NPC data), monsters (dict of monster ID to monster data), start_room (str). Each room has name (str), description (str), connections (dict of direction to room ID), items (list of item IDs), npcs (list of NPC IDs), monsters (list of monster IDs). Each item has name (str), type (str: weapon/armor/healing/key), stats (dict of stat modifiers), description (str). Each NPC has name (str), dialogue (list of str), quest_flags (list of str). Each monster has name (str), health (int), attack (int), behavior (str: aggressive/passive/guard), loot (list of item IDs), optional phases (list of phase dicts for boss).
data_shapes.example:
rooms:
  village_square:
    name: Village Square
    description: A quiet cobblestone square.
    connections:
      north: forest_path
      east: shop
    items: []
    npcs: [elder]
    monsters: []
items:
  rusty_sword:
    name: Rusty Sword
    type: weapon
    stats:
      attack_bonus: 2
    description: A dented old sword.
npcs:
  elder:
    name: Village Elder
    dialogue:
      - "Welcome, traveler."
      - "The Crystal Shard in the cave is the only weakness of the Shadow Lord."
    quest_flags: [knows_weakness]
monsters:
  goblin:
    name: Goblin
    health: 10
    attack: 2
    behavior: aggressive
    loot: []
start_room: village_square

architecture.notes: Flat layout eliminates package complexity. All game content is data-driven via world.yaml for easy modding. State is centralized in GameEngine to avoid desync. Combat uses equipment-modified stats, boss has two health-phase triggers with unique behavior, Crystal Shard (boss weakness) deals 3x damage. NPC dialogue provides explicit hints to locate the weakness item. Save files use human-readable JSON format.
